# postgrelize usage guide (for LLMs and agents)

`@tormozz48/postgrelize` is a PostgreSQL-only ORM for Node.js and TypeScript. It implements the **Sequelize v6 public API** (same names, options, return values, error classes, hook order), so Sequelize v6 knowledge and code carry over. On top of that it adds PostgreSQL features as **new** options and methods (`onConflict`, `Model.insert`, `merge`, CTEs, `copyFrom`, `listen`, advisory locks, `returningOld`). It never changes v6 semantics.

This file is generated from code that is type-checked and run in CI (`docs/examples/llm-usage.ts` and the other `docs/examples/*.ts`), so every snippet compiles and works against the current version. Types are in the package's `.d.ts` files (`node_modules/@tormozz48/postgrelize/dist/index.d.ts`); every public item there has TSDoc.

Requirements: Node.js 20+, PostgreSQL 16/17/18, the `pg` package (peer dependency).

## Install

The package lives on GitHub Packages. Add to `.npmrc`:

```ini
@tormozz48:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com
//npm.pkg.github.com/:_authToken=${GITHUB_TOKEN}
```

Install under the alias `postgrelize` so imports read `from 'postgrelize'` (all snippets below use that):

```bash
npm install postgrelize@npm:@tormozz48/postgrelize pg
```

ES modules and CommonJS are both shipped. Without the alias, import from `'@tormozz48/postgrelize'`.

## Imports used in the snippets

```ts
import {
  AllowNull,
  Column,
  DataTypes,
  DatabaseError,
  ForeignKey,
  HasMany,
  Model,
  Op,
  PrimaryKey,
  AutoIncrement,
  QueryTypes,
  Sequelize,
  Table,
  UniqueConstraintError,
  ValidationError,
  col,
  fn,
  literal,
} from 'postgrelize';
import type { CreationOptional, InferAttributes, InferCreationAttributes } from 'postgrelize';
```

## Connect

```ts
export const openConnection = (url: string): Sequelize =>
  new Sequelize(url, { logging: false, pool: { max: 10 } });
// call `await sequelize.authenticate()` to check it; `await sequelize.close()` on shutdown
```

Create **one** `Sequelize` instance per database. It accepts a URI, `(database, user, password, options)`, or an options object (`host`, `port`, `database`, `username`, `password`, `ssl`, `pool`, `dialectOptions` passed to `pg`, `replication: { read, write }`, `timezone` default `'+00:00'`). `dialect` may be omitted; anything but `'postgres'` throws. Connection failures are `ConnectionError` subclasses.

## Define models

Three equivalent styles. Types: `InferAttributes`, `InferCreationAttributes`, `CreationOptional`, `ForeignKey`, `NonAttribute`.

Class + `init` (typed):

```ts
class User extends Model<InferAttributes<User>, InferCreationAttributes<User>> {
  declare id: CreationOptional<number>;
  declare email: string;
  declare active: CreationOptional<boolean>;
}

User.init(
  {
    id: { type: DataTypes.INTEGER, primaryKey: true, autoIncrement: true },
    email: { type: DataTypes.STRING, allowNull: false, unique: true },
    active: { type: DataTypes.BOOLEAN, allowNull: false, defaultValue: true },
  },
  { sequelize, tableName: 'llm_users' },
);
```

`sequelize.define` (untyped attributes, returns a model class):

```ts
const Note = sequelize.define(
  'Note',
  { text: DataTypes.TEXT, meta: DataTypes.JSONB, tags: DataTypes.ARRAY(DataTypes.TEXT) },
  { tableName: 'llm_notes', paranoid: true },
);
```

Decorators (TC39 or legacy signatures; register with `sequelize.addModels`):

```ts
@Table({ tableName: 'llm_teams' })
class Team extends Model {
  @PrimaryKey
  @AutoIncrement
  @Column(DataTypes.INTEGER)
  id!: number;

  @AllowNull(false)
  @Column(DataTypes.TEXT)
  name!: string;

  @HasMany(() => Player)
  players?: Player[];
}

@Table({ tableName: 'llm_players' })
class Player extends Model {
  @PrimaryKey
  @AutoIncrement
  @Column(DataTypes.INTEGER)
  id!: number;

  @Column(DataTypes.TEXT)
  nick!: string;

  @ForeignKey(() => Team)
  @Column(DataTypes.INTEGER)
  teamId!: number;
}

sequelize.addModels([Team, Player]);
```

Common model options: `tableName`, `freezeTableName`, `schema`, `timestamps` (default `true`: `createdAt`/`updatedAt`), `paranoid` (soft delete with `deletedAt`), `underscored`, `version` (optimistic locking, `OptimisticLockError`), `indexes`, `hooks`, `scopes`, `defaultScope`, `validate`. Data types: `DataTypes.INTEGER`, `BIGINT` (returned as string), `DECIMAL` (string), `TEXT`, `STRING(n)`, `BOOLEAN`, `DATE` (timestamptz), `UUID`, `JSONB`, `ARRAY(type)`, `ENUM(...)`, range types, `GEOMETRY` for DDL.

Create tables with `await sequelize.sync()` (tests, prototypes). For production use migrations through `sequelize.getQueryInterface()` (see Schema).

## CRUD cheat sheet

```ts
const ann = await User.create({ email: 'ann@example.com' });
await User.bulkCreate([
  { email: 'bob@example.com' },
  { email: 'eve@example.com', active: false },
]);

const byKey = await User.findByPk(ann.id);
const one = await User.findOne({ where: { email: 'bob@example.com' } });
const [cid, created] = await User.findOrCreate({
  where: { email: 'cid@example.com' },
  defaults: { active: true },
});
const all = await User.findAll({ where: { active: true }, order: [['email', 'ASC']], limit: 10 });
const total = await User.count();

ann.active = false; // change tracking: save() writes only changed attributes
await ann.save();
await ann.update({ email: 'ann@corp.example.com' });
await ann.reload();
await User.update({ active: true }, { where: { email: { [Op.like]: '%@example.com' } } });
await User.destroy({ where: { id: cid.id } }); // paranoid models soft-delete; { force: true } removes
```

Also available as in v6: `findAndCountAll`, `findOrBuild`, `build` + `save`, `bulkCreate`, `restore`, `increment`/`decrement`, `instance.destroy()`, `instance.set()`/`get()`/`changed()`, `toJSON()`. `rejectOnEmpty: true` makes finders throw `EmptyResultError` instead of returning `null`. `raw: true` returns plain objects; `nest: true` nests dotted keys.

Nested creation: `Model.create(values, { include: [{ association: 'posts' }] })` where `values` contains the nested array. Nested values are not creation attributes in the types, so pass `values` as a variable, not an object literal.

## Where, operators, query options

```ts
const matches = await Note.findAll({
  where: {
    [Op.and]: [
      { text: { [Op.iLike]: '%pg%' } },
      { [Op.or]: [{ 'meta.level': 'info' }, { tags: { [Op.contains]: ['sql'] } }] },
      { id: { [Op.notIn]: [0, -1] } },
    ],
  },
});
// other operators: Op.eq ne gt gte lt lte between in is not like notLike regexp overlap
// contains contained hasKey any all isDistinctFrom; compare columns with col('other')
```

`Op` has all v6 operators plus PostgreSQL ones. Write JSON paths as dotted keys (`'meta.level'`) or nested objects. Compare columns with `col('name')`. `where(fn/col, Op.x, value)` builds comparisons on expressions.

```ts
const { count, rows } = await Note.findAndCountAll({
  attributes: ['id', 'text'],
  order: [['id', 'DESC']],
  limit: 1,
  offset: 0,
  raw: true,
});
const perTag = await Note.findAll({
  attributes: [
    [fn('unnest', col('tags')), 'tag'],
    [fn('count', col('id')), 'n'],
  ],
  group: ['tag'],
  raw: true,
});
const sum = await Note.sum('id');
await Note.destroy({ where: { text: 'misc' } }); // soft delete, the row stays with deletedAt set
const withDeleted = await Note.findAll({ paranoid: false });
```

Other options: `attributes: { include, exclude }`, `include`, `distinct`, `group`, `having`, `lock`, `transaction`, `paranoid`, `logging`, `benchmark`, scopes via `Model.scope('name')` / `Model.scope({ method: ['name', arg] })`, `findEach` / `findAll` with `limit`/`offset`, keyset pagination with `where(tuple(col('rank'), col('id')), Op.lt, tuple(3, 1))`.

## Associations and include

`hasOne`, `hasMany`, `belongsTo`, `belongsToMany` work as in v6 and generate accessors (`getPosts`, `addTag`, `createPost`, `countPosts`, ...). Declare accessor types with `declare` on the class when using TypeScript.

```ts
const team = await Team.create({ name: 'blue' });
await Player.create({ nick: 'ace', teamId: team.id });
const teams = await Team.findAll({
  include: [{ association: 'players', required: true, attributes: ['nick'] }],
});
// teams[0].players?.[0].nick === 'ace'; accessors such as team.getPlayers() are generated too
```

Include options: `association` (or `model` + `as`), `where`, `required`, `right`, `attributes`, nested `include`, `separate`, `through`, `paranoid`, `all: true`. Eager loading uses JOINs like v6.

## Transactions

Managed (commit on resolve, rollback on throw) and explicit:

```ts
const placed = await sequelize.transaction(async (transaction) => {
  const user = await User.create({ email: 'tx@example.com' }, { transaction });
  await Note.create({ text: `for ${user.email}` }, { transaction });
  return user.id; // commits when the callback resolves, rolls back when it throws
});

const manual = await sequelize.transaction();
try {
  await User.update({ active: false }, { where: { id: placed }, transaction: manual });
  await manual.commit();
} catch (error) {
  await manual.rollback();
  throw error;
}
```

Pass `{ transaction }` to every query that must take part. Nested `sequelize.transaction({ transaction: outer }, fn)` creates a savepoint. Options: `isolationLevel: Transaction.ISOLATION_LEVELS.REPEATABLE_READ`, `readOnly: true`, `settings: { 'app.user_id': 42 }` (SET LOCAL). Row locks: `lock: true` or `Transaction.LOCK.UPDATE`, `skipLocked`, `noWait`. Hooks after commit: `transaction.afterCommit(fn)`.

CLS (implicit transaction in callbacks, a **process-wide** switch, uses `AsyncLocalStorage`, no namespace argument):

```ts
Sequelize.useCLS(); // global switch: managed transactions now apply to queries inside the callback
await sequelize.transaction(async () => {
  await User.update({ active: true }, { where: {} }); // runs in the transaction, no option needed
});
```

## Hooks and validation

```ts
const log: string[] = [];
User.beforeCreate((user: User) => {
  user.email = user.email.toLowerCase();
});
User.addHook('afterUpdate', 'log-update', (user: User) => {
  log.push(`updated ${user.id}`);
});
const mixed = await User.create({ email: 'MiXed@Example.com' });
await mixed.update({ active: false });
```

Hook order for `create`: `beforeValidate`, `afterValidate` (or `validationFailed`), `beforeCreate`, `afterCreate`. Updates use `beforeUpdate`/`afterUpdate`; also `beforeSave`/`afterSave`, `beforeDestroy`, `beforeUpsert`, `beforeBulkCreate`, `beforeFind`, `afterFind`. Bulk operations run row hooks only with `individualHooks: true`; `hooks: false` skips hooks for one call. Only model lifecycle hooks and `beforeConnect` are executed; connection, sync and define hooks (`afterConnect`, `beforeSync`, `beforeDefine`, ...) are accepted but never called.

Validators in attribute definitions work as in v6 (`validate: { isEmail: true, len: [2, 50] }`, custom functions, model-level `validate`). Extra: `validate: { schema: z.email() }` and model option `validationSchema` accept any Standard Schema library (zod, valibot, arktype).

## Upserts, ON CONFLICT, RETURNING

```ts
const [row] = await User.upsert({ id: ann.id, email: 'ann@corp.example.com', active: true });
// v6 shape: [instance, null]; pass onConflict to get a real inserted/updated boolean
const [visit, wasInserted] = await User.upsert(
  { email: 'new@example.com' },
  { onConflict: { target: ['email'], action: { update: { active: true } } } },
);
const written = await User.insert(
  [{ email: 'new@example.com' }, { email: 'other@example.com' }],
  { onConflict: { target: ['email'], action: 'nothing' } },
); // returns the rows that were actually inserted
const [changed, updated = []] = await User.update(
  { active: false },
  { where: { email: 'new@example.com' }, returning: true },
);
```

- v6 `upsert` returns `[instance, null]` (PostgreSQL does not say whether it inserted). Pass `onConflict` to get a boolean.
- `onConflict: { target: ['a', 'b'] | { constraint } | { columns, where }, action: 'nothing' | { update: ['col'] | { col: expression }, where } }` works in `upsert`, `bulkCreate`, `Model.insert`. Expressions: `excluded('col')`, `literal(...)`, `fn(...)`, `col(...)`. `Model.insert` returns instances with `wasInserted`.
- `returning: true` on `update` / `destroy` returns instances. `returningOld: true` adds `instance.oldValues` (PostgreSQL 18+ only).
- v6 `bulkCreate` options `updateOnDuplicate` with `conflictAttributes`, and `ignoreDuplicates`, still work.

More: `Model.update(values, { where, from: { d: Delivery } })` (UPDATE ... FROM), `Model.destroy({ where, using })`, `Model.insertFrom(subquery, { columns })`, `Model.merge({ source, on, whenMatched, whenNotMatched, whenNotMatchedBySource, returning })` (MERGE, PostgreSQL 17+ for `returning`):

Example: `docs/examples/merge-returning.ts` in the repository (`Stock.merge({ source: [{ sku: 'a', qty: 3 }], on: { sku: col('source.sku') }, whenMatched: { update: { qty: col('source.qty') } }, whenNotMatched: { insert: true }, returning: true })` resolves to `{ rows: [{ action, instance }] }`).

## Subqueries, CTEs, windows

`Model.subquery(findOptions)` builds an embeddable SELECT (use in `Op.in`, attributes, `exists()`). `with: { name: { query, recursive?, materialized? } }` adds CTEs to finders/`count`; `source: 'cte'` reads from one. Window functions through `over(...)`; `distinctOn`. Recursive CTE example: `docs/examples/advanced-queries.ts` (region `recursive-cte`) in the repository.

## COPY, listen/notify, locks

```ts
const fromArray = await Event.copyFrom([
  { kind: 'signup', payload: { plan: 'pro' }, tags: ['web'] },
  { kind: 'login', payload: null, tags: null },
]);

const fromStream = await Event.copyFrom(readEvents(), { columns: ['kind', 'payload'] });
// fromArray === 2, fromStream === 1000; createdAt / updatedAt are filled in
```

`Model.copyTo(options)` streams `COPY ... TO STDOUT` (async iterable of Buffer). `await sequelize.listen('channel', (payload) => ...)` returns an `unlisten` function; `sequelize.notify(channel, payload, { transaction })` delivers on commit. `transaction.advisoryLock(key)` / `tryAdvisoryLock(key)` take transaction-level advisory locks; `sequelize.withAdvisoryLock(key, fn)` runs `fn` in a transaction holding the lock.

## Raw queries

```ts
const found = (await sequelize.query('SELECT id FROM llm_users WHERE email = :email', {
  replacements: { email: 'ann@corp.example.com' },
  type: QueryTypes.SELECT,
})) as { id: number }[];
const ordered = await User.findAll({ order: [literal('"email" DESC NULLS LAST')] });
```

`sequelize.query(sql, { replacements | bind, type: QueryTypes.SELECT, plain, raw, transaction })`. `replacements` use `:name` or `?`, `bind` uses `$1` / `$name`. Set `type: QueryTypes.SELECT` to get the rows array directly.

## Schema, sync, migrations

```ts
export const up = async (queryInterface: QueryInterface): Promise<void> => {
  await queryInterface.createTable('accounts', {
    id: { type: DataTypes.BIGINT, primaryKey: true, autoIncrement: true },
    email: { type: DataTypes.TEXT, allowNull: false, unique: true },
    plan: { type: DataTypes.ENUM('free', 'pro'), allowNull: false, defaultValue: 'free' },
    created_at: { type: DataTypes.DATE, allowNull: false, defaultValue: DataTypes.NOW },
  });
  await queryInterface.createTable('sessions', {
    id: { type: DataTypes.UUID, primaryKey: true },
    account_id: {
      type: DataTypes.BIGINT,
      allowNull: false,
      references: { model: 'accounts', key: 'id', deferrable: Deferrable.INITIALLY_DEFERRED },
      onDelete: 'CASCADE',
    },
  });
  await queryInterface.addIndex('sessions', ['account_id']);
  await queryInterface.addColumn('accounts', 'note', { type: DataTypes.TEXT });
};

export const down = async (queryInterface: QueryInterface): Promise<void> => {
  await queryInterface.dropTable('sessions');
  await queryInterface.dropTable('accounts');
  await queryInterface.dropEnum('enum_accounts_plan');
};
```

`sequelize.sync()` creates missing tables; `{ alter: true }` adjusts columns; `{ force: true }` drops first (never in production). `sequelize.getQueryInterface()` offers `createTable`, `dropTable`, `addColumn`, `removeColumn`, `changeColumn`, `addIndex`, `addConstraint`, `describeTable`, `showAllTables`, `tableExists`, `dropEnum`, `bulkInsert`, ... Indexes in model options support `unique`, `where` (partial), `using`, `nullsNotDistinct`. `describeTable`, `showAllTables` and `tableExists` default to `current_schema()`.

## Errors to catch

All are exported classes, as in v6.

```ts
const duplicate = await User.create({ email: 'new@example.com' }).catch(
  (error: unknown) => error,
);
const invalid = await User.create({ email: null as unknown as string }).catch(
  (error: unknown) => error,
);
const bad = await sequelize
  .query('SELECT * FROM "no_such_table"')
  .catch((error: unknown) => error);
// UniqueConstraintError and ValidationError extend ValidationError/BaseError; DatabaseError wraps
// any other server error: `error.parent` holds the pg error with `code`, `detail`, `constraint`
```

| Class | When |
| --- | --- |
| `ValidationError` (`.errors[]` of `ValidationErrorItem`) | validators, `allowNull`, schema validation |
| `UniqueConstraintError`, `ForeignKeyConstraintError`, `ExclusionConstraintError` | constraint violation (SQLSTATE 23xxx) |
| `DatabaseError` (`.parent`, `.sql`) | any other server error (syntax, read-only transaction, lock not available, ...) |
| `OptimisticLockError` | stale `version` on save |
| `EmptyResultError` | `rejectOnEmpty` found nothing |
| `ConnectionError` and subclasses (`ConnectionRefusedError`, `ConnectionTimedOutError`, `AccessDeniedError`, ...) | cannot reach or authenticate |
| `TimeoutError` | statement or query timeout |
| `BaseError` | parent of all of them |

## Top mistakes

1. **Forgetting `transaction`.** Queries without `{ transaction }` run on another connection and do not see uncommitted rows (unless CLS is on).
2. **Mixing the import path.** With the alias, import from `'postgrelize'`; without it from `'@tormozz48/postgrelize'`. Do not install `sequelize` next to it.
3. **Expecting `upsert` to report insert vs update.** It returns `[instance, null]`; use `onConflict`.
4. **`BIGINT` / `DECIMAL` are strings** in results. Convert explicitly.
5. **Using `sync()` as a migration tool in production.** Use `QueryInterface` migrations.
6. **Building SQL from user input** (see Security). Use `where`, `replacements`, `bind`.
7. **Using other dialects or v7 API** (`@sequelize/core`). Only PostgreSQL and the v6 API exist.
8. **Using hooks outside the model lifecycle** (`afterConnect`, `beforeSync`, ...). They are never called.
9. **`Sequelize.useCLS()` is global.** Call it once at startup, not per instance.
10. **`create(values, { ignoreDuplicates })`** is not supported; use `onConflict: { action: 'nothing' }` or `bulkCreate(..., { ignoreDuplicates })`.

## Differences from Sequelize v6

postgrelize fixes v6 bugs on PostgreSQL instead of copying them (JSON `where` keys with special characters, `upsert` on partial unique indexes, `sync({ alter })` sequences, schema-aware `describeTable`, `Op.any` shorthand, unchecked function names and isolation levels, and more). The full list with issue numbers: <https://tormozz48.github.io/postgrelize/sequelize-issues>. Migration notes: <https://tormozz48.github.io/postgrelize/guide/migrating>.

Not available from v6: other dialects, `minifyAliases`, `Model.schema('tenant')` (use the `schema` option or `search_path` via `dialectOptions: { options: '-c search_path=tenant' }`), the `searchPath` option, named/shared `ENUM` types (each `ENUM` column gets `enum_<table>_<column>`), `create({ ignoreDuplicates })`.

## PostgreSQL features that are NOT supported

Source of truth: <https://tormozz48.github.io/postgrelize/postgresql-coverage> (generated from `docs/coverage/postgresql-features.ts`). "Planned" and "out of scope" rows; most can be done with `sequelize.query()` raw SQL or `literal()`:

- **SELECT clauses**: Data-modifying CTEs (WITH … UPDATE/DELETE … RETURNING); CTE SEARCH / CYCLE clauses; LATERAL joins; TABLESAMPLE; FETCH FIRST … WITH TIES; UNION / INTERSECT / EXCEPT [ALL]; Standalone VALUES lists and set-returning functions in FROM (unnest, generate_series, WITH ORDINALITY); ONLY (table inheritance)
- **Operators and functions**: JSON_TABLE; Multirange operators and functions (range_agg, unnest); Geometric operators and functions; hstore operators (->, ?, @>); ltree operators (@>, <@, ~, ?)
- **Data types**: timestamp without time zone; money; composite types; multirange types; xml; bit and bit varying; macaddr8; geometric types (point, line, lseg, box, path, polygon, circle); tsquery; pg_lsn, txid_snapshot and other system types; hstore (extension); ltree (extension); PostGIS geometry / geography
- **DDL (sync and QueryInterface)**: EXCLUDE constraints; NOT VALID constraints and VALIDATE CONSTRAINT; NOT ENFORCED constraints, WITHOUT OVERLAPS keys, FK PERIOD; Expression indexes (lower(email)); Views and materialized views; Sequences (CREATE SEQUENCE, setval); Functions and triggers; Declarative partitioning (PARTITION BY / PARTITION OF / ATTACH); Extensions (CREATE EXTENSION); Row-level security policies; UNLOGGED and TEMPORARY tables; Rules (CREATE RULE)
- **Session features**: Two-phase commit (PREPARE TRANSACTION)
- **Out of scope**: Roles, GRANT / REVOKE, default privileges; Replication setup (publications, subscriptions, slots, logical decoding); Tablespaces; VACUUM, ANALYZE, REINDEX, CLUSTER, pg_stat views; Procedural languages (PL/pgSQL bodies, DO blocks, procedures); Extension internals (writing or configuring extensions); Foreign data wrappers and foreign tables; Server configuration (ALTER SYSTEM, pg_hba.conf, event triggers)

## Security rules

- **Values are always bound** (`$1..$n`) in `where`, `create`, `update`, `upsert`, `insert`, `merge`, `replacements`, `bind`, `NOTIFY` payloads, advisory keys and `settings`. Never concatenate user input into SQL text.
- **Identifiers** (column, table, alias, schema, channel names) are quoted. Operators, function names, cast types, lock strengths, isolation levels and `order` directions are checked against allowlists and throw on anything else. If a column name comes from a user, map it through your own allowlist anyway.
- **`literal()`, raw `sequelize.query` text and string `where` are raw by design** and not escaped. Use them only with constants you wrote.

Full table of inputs and protections: <https://tormozz48.github.io/postgrelize/security>.

## Verify by running

Run the code against a real PostgreSQL (`docker run -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=pw -p 5432:5432 postgres:17`) and read the result; do not assume a query works. Log SQL with `new Sequelize(url, { logging: console.log })`. When unsure about a signature, read the TSDoc in `node_modules/@tormozz48/postgrelize/dist/*.d.ts` or the API reference at <https://tormozz48.github.io/postgrelize/api/>. Full documentation for LLMs: <https://tormozz48.github.io/postgrelize/llms.txt> and <https://tormozz48.github.io/postgrelize/llms-full.txt>.
